mmf.total_aum_wow_note: This is the change in TOTAL industry AUM week-over-week -- it is NOT a measure of net Treasury purchases. Inflows can sit in repo or agency paper rather than bills/notes.
mmf.government_fund_aum_note: Government/Treasury funds are the largest MMF subclass by AUM. This is a buyer-BASE size, not a measure of actual Treasury securities held -- government funds also hold repo (often Treasury-collateralized but not itself a Treasury security) and agency debt.
mmf.treasury_holdings_note: The ICI weekly release does not break out direct Treasury bill/note/bond holdings within government funds separately from repo and agency exposure. Actual $ of Treasury securities held by MMFs is not yet wired into this pipeline.
mmf.net_treasury_purchases_note: Marginal net Treasury purchases by MMFs this week cannot be measured from AUM changes alone. Not fabricated -- shown as PENDING until a flow-based source (e.g., Treasury OFR MMF holdings detail, or SEC N-MFP) is integrated.

to_risk_off: Group A (Duration/Treasury): STRESS-type bear steepening, or Long-End Stress Confirmed (30Y>5.5% + a confirming signal), or auction tails, or dealer take-down rising

OR Group C (Credit): HY/IG spreads widen materially

key_takeaways: Regime: CONTROLLED TIGHTENING / LIQUIDITY PROTECTED (PROVISIONAL) -- Monetary Restrictiveness 68/100 (HIGH, unchanged), Liquidity Resilience 64/100 (MODERATE-HIGH, IMPROVING as Korea gate margin widens and credit proxies firm).

Korea gate HOLDS OPEN at 3/3, and the margin widens back out sharply -- EWY (188.40, +3.91%) now sits 6.76 above its SMA20 (181.64); KOSPI (7,007.73, +1.65%) clears its 5-day SMA comfortably; USDKRW (1,374.40) firms further, well below 1,530.

VIX continues to ease (-0.67% to 14.72) while MOVE stays pinned above its 80 stress-watch line, unchanged from Friday's close at 80.64 -- not a fresh deterioration, but not resolving either; the key overhang heading into tomorrow's 2Y auction.

Oil extends its slide sharply, -3.89% to $92.34, crossing the -3% single-day threshold again -- still not confirmed by breakevens (T5YIE/T10YIE both unchanged from Friday); DFII5 (primary real yield) also stays flat at 2.46% for a second session.

Regime confidence falls to 42% (base 55%, -8% for the Sep 22-24 auction trio starting within 48h, -5% for MOVE staying above 80) -- lower than Friday's 50%, driven by the imminent auction catalyst rather than any fresh deterioration.

v2.auction_core_question: Can private markets continue absorbing duration while monetary policy remains restrictive, without destabilizing the long end?
v2.auction_summary_verdict: HISTORICAL: the seven most recent auctions (10Y Aug 12, 30Y Aug 13, 20Y Aug 19, 3Y Sep 8, 10Y Sep 9, 30Y Sep 10, and 20Y Sep 15) -- the first six cleared cleanly with no tails; the Sep 8-10 cycle's two REGIME VALIDATION tests were the strongest of the stretch (10Y Sep 9: BTC 2.71, dealer 4.3%, indirect 79.0%; 30Y Sep 10: BTC 2.61, dealer 2.2%, indirect 79.3%), but the Sep 15 20Y reopening reversed that trend sharply -- dealer take-down 16.7% (100th pctile), indirect 52.1% (5th pctile), the weakest demand mix in the ledger. FORWARD: the next REGIME VALIDATION test is the 9Y10M TIPS reopening on Sep 17, one day after today's FOMC decision -- it will confirm or reverse whether the weak 20Y print was a one-off or the start of a trend.
